issues.description: The Farm.singFarmSong() method and its helper singFarmSongVerse(Animal) have conflicting return-type contracts across artifacts. The problem statement UML (Farm: + singFarmSong(): void) and the template Farm.java declare singFarmSong() as void and provide a private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/) stub that prints the verse. The solution repository implements these as returning String (private String singFarmSongVerse(Animal) and public String singFarmSong()) and returns the composed song text instead of printing it. This mismatch (void/printing vs. String/returning) will confuse students about whether they should print the song or return it and may cause automated tests or grader scripts that expect printing to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method contracts consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: update the solution to match the UML/template by changing singFarmSong() to return void and singFarmSongVerse(Animal) to be a private void that prints the verse lines directly (so behavior and signatures align with the problem statement and template). Alternative: if the course prefers returning the full song text, update the problem statement UML and the template method signatures to declare singFarmSong(): String (and singFarmSongVerse returning String) and document that tests will consume the returned String. Ensure tests/grader and examples reflect the chosen contract.
